question: Prove that corrugation has returned between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green.
norm_question: prove that corrugation has returned between liverpool street and bethnal green

answer.text: Our evidence cannot show whether corrugation has re-formed between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green because we hold no rail roughness data for that section and our phone loudness check was NO-GO (triggered by a -0.13 dB trip reversal).

verified_claims.text: The evidence we hold cannot show whether corrugation has re-formed between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green because no rail roughness data is held for that section; the rail roughness plots in FOI-1730-1819 (published 22 October 2018) cover only 'Eastbound Bethnal Green to Mile End'.

citations.quote: Eastbound Bethnal Green to Mile End
Date published: 22 October 2018

verified_claims.text: Our phone recordings only measure uncalibrated relative acoustic levels and yielded a NO-GO verdict on the pre-registered loudness check between Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green and Bethnal Green to Mile End because one westbound trip went the other way (-0.13 dB), with the +0.54 dB mean difference over 11 trips also below the 1 dB threshold and level variants not agreeing.

The Mayor's written answer to Question 2022/1791 lists 'Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street' (without stating a direction) among sections that benefited from noise-related rail grinding between December 2021 and May 2022, and TfL Head of Track Duncan Weir's letter of 9 December 2022 lists 'Liverpool Street - Bethnal Green Eastbound Central' for deep Tube reconditioning planned for financial year 2023/24.
